We face Regulatory Approval Risk in relation to a Customer Contract

 

Our operations involve the provision of high-performance computing infrastructure and software, including advanced GPUs and related services, which may have dual-use applications.

 

As a result, certain activities and customer contracts entered into by the Company may be subject to regulation under the Defence Trade Controls Act 2012 (Cth), the Weapons of Mass Destruction (Prevention of Proliferation) Act 1995 (Cth), and other applicable export laws relating to import, export, re-export or transfer controls, restrictions, trade and economic sanctions laws and regulations, including without limitation, administered or enforced by any government or intergovernmental organisation, including Australia, the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom, the United Nations and China, including any implementing rules, regulations, orders and notices issued under those applicable laws (Trade Laws).

 

Customer contracts under which services may be accessed or utilised by foreign nationals or across multiple jurisdictions, are subject to certain Trade Laws which may require the Company to obtain permits, licences, consents, approvals and authorisations, or otherwise comply with those laws. Failure to obtain any required permits, licences, consents, approvals, authorisations or other permissions in a timely manner, may restrict or prohibit the Company from providing services to its customers potentially entitling the customer to suspend or terminate the contract in accordance with its terms. If any such customer contract is terminated as a result of the Company’s failure to obtain the necessary permits, licences, approvals or authorisations required under applicable Trade Laws, this could have a material adverse effect on the Company’s financial performance and financial position, particularly if the Company is unable to re-contract the relevant GPU capacity to alternative customers on comparable terms.

 

The Company may be required to perform customer due diligence, obtain end-user certifications, limit or refuse service to certain customers, suspend or terminate existing customer arrangements, or restructure aspects of its business model in order to comply with applicable Trade Laws.

 

Failure to comply with Trade Laws could result in civil or criminal penalties, loss of licences or permits, reputational damage, and/or restrictions on the Company’s ability to provide services to certain customers or in certain jurisdictions. In addition, compliance obligations may increase the Company’s operational complexity and costs, and could adversely impact its ability to scale its business.

We Face Financing Risk of Secured Customer Contracts

 

We have signed material customer contracts with ESDS, a Global Technology Customer, and a Global AI Lab Customer and Nvidia. For the Global Technology Customer Contract, the Company has recently secured a US$356 million GPU-backed SPV debt financing facility at a fixed interest rate of 9.95% (excluding fees and other one-off charges) and continues to engage with potential financiers regarding additional debt funding arrangements for the other customer deployments. The Company is engaging with potential debt financiers for a proposed partial debt financing, required under its customer contracts in order to deliver services under those contracts. However, no binding financing arrangements have been finalised or locked in as at the date of this document.

 

To the extent that the debt financing being sought is not able to be achieved (or on acceptable terms), the Company would be required to source alternative financing arrangements (which may include a combination of alternative debt structures, equipment financing, equity capital or other funding sources) in order to fund the purchase of GPUs and associated hardware necessary to meet its contractual obligations under the ESDS and Global AI Lab Customer Contracts. There can be no assurance that such alternative financing would be available on acceptable terms, or at all, which may impact the timing, economics or delivery of the contract, which may have a material adverse effect on the Company’s financial condition.

 

In addition, the interest and other costs associated with any financing ultimately secured will be influenced by the amount, structure and timing of funding drawdowns, prevailing interest rate conditions, lender credit risk assessment, and the final terms agreed with financing counterparties. Outside the NVIDIA Collaboration Agreement, the Company’s three largest customer contracts are with ESDS, the Global Technology Customer and the Global AI Lab Customer so it is highly exposed to the credit quality of each one and reliant on each party to adhere to the terms of their contracts. Further, there may also be complexity and challenges in enforcing contractual rights against its customers located offshore (including if enforcement is subject to foreign laws, regulatory requirements or court processes). The Company has assessed and diligenced its contract counterparties including their ability to meet contract and payment obligations, and remains comfortable with these arrangements based on the current market conditions and appetite. If a material customer terminated or did not meet its obligations under the respective contracts, there may be significant risk of a material adverse effect on the Company’s financial performance and financial condition. In circumstances where those contracts are terminated, the Company may seek to enter into arrangements with alternative customers. However, there can be no assurance that any such new customer contracts could be secured on terms that are similar to those contained in the ESDS Contract, the Global Technology Customer or the Global AI Lab Customer Contract, which may adversely affect the Company’s revenues, profitability and cashflows.

 

Our September 2026 Secured GPU Infrastructure Financing Exposes us to Debt-Service, Refinancing and Collateral-Enforcement Risks that Could Materially Adversely Affect our Business, Financial Condition and Results of Operations.

 

In September 2026, our Australian subsidiaries (the “Borrowers”) have entered into a senior secured facility agreement with Global Loan Agency Services Australia Specialist Activities Pty Limited, as agent (the “Agent”), Global Loan Agency Services Australia Nominees Pty Ltd, as security trustee and the other lenders party thereto providing for up to US$356 million of term loan financing to finance and refinance servers, GPUs and related infrastructure supporting a customer contract for GPU compute capacity. The facility comprises Facility A of up to US$150 million and Facility B of up to US$206 million. Borrowings require monthly cash interest payments, with Facility A bearing an initial fixed rate of 7.25% per annum that increases on specified dates to as much as 9.95%, and Facility B bearing a fixed rate of 9.95% per annum. Each facility matures 42 months after its first utilization, when the remaining principal is repayable in a lump sum, subject to mandatory prepayments. These obligations could require us to devote substantial cash resources to debt service, reducing funds available for operations, capital expenditures and growth.

 

Our ability to service and repay these borrowings depends on the timely deployment and operation of the financed infrastructure, customer acceptance and receipt of payments under the related customer arrangements. Deployment delays, operational interruptions, customer payment defaults or termination of the customer contract could reduce or delay the cash flows available to meet our financing obligations without a corresponding reduction in those obligations. Delays in customer acceptance could also delay the anticipated application of a customer deposit held in escrow to repay Facility A and the expected release of our parent-company guarantee. We cannot assure investors that project cash flows, customer payments or other available resources will be sufficient to meet debt service or repay the remaining principal at maturity, or that refinancing will be available when required on acceptable terms, if at all.

 

-43-

 

 

The Facility Agreement requires the Borrowers to comply with a quarterly gross loan-to-value covenant, subject to limited equity cure rights. Technological advances, the introduction of newer GPUs, reduced demand for the financed equipment or declines in its market value could impair covenant compliance even if the equipment remains operational and customer payments continue. Compliance with the applicable covenant limits, including scheduled step-downs, could require additional equity funding or debt reduction at a time when capital is unavailable or available only on unfavorable terms. We cannot assure investors that a covenant breach could be cured or that the lenders would grant a waiver or amendment.

 

The Facility Agreement also provides for mandatory prepayments from specified asset disposal proceeds, insurance proceeds and certain customer contract termination payments, which could limit the cash available to replace assets, restore operations or pursue other business needs. Facility B may not be voluntarily prepaid until Facility A has been repaid in full, and specified prepayments and acceleration of Facility B during the first 18 months following utilization are subject to a make-whole premium. These provisions could increase the cost of refinancing, restructuring or exiting the financing. In addition, a loss of our 100% ownership and control of the Borrowers, or a Borrower default under the relevant customer contract giving rise to a termination right, constitutes a review event, potentially complicating strategic transactions or the resolution of customer disputes.

 

The financing is secured by substantially all assets of the Borrowers and their immediate holding companies, including equity interests, project bank accounts and rights under material project contracts, subject to applicable protections. Upon an event of default, including payment default, financial covenant breach, cross-default or specified material contract defaults, the Agent may cancel commitments, accelerate outstanding amounts and enforce the transaction security. Enforcement could result in the loss of financed equipment, project cash flows and control of the relevant subsidiaries, materially impairing our ability to provide services and generate revenue. We have also guaranteed the Borrowers’ payment obligations under both facilities, subject to the applicable release and termination provisions. We may therefore be required to fund those obligations while that guarantee remains effective. Although the financing is expected to become non-recourse to us following repayment of Facility A, subject to the arrangements described in the Facility Agreement summary, that transition would not eliminate the risk of losing our investment in the relevant subsidiaries or the adverse operational consequences of enforcement. Any of these events could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations.

Not all Events that May Adversely Affect the Trading Price of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and the June 2026 Convertible Notes and our Class A Ordinary Common Stock will Result in an Adjustment to the Conversion Rate.

  ● certain stock dividends, splits and combinations;
     
  ● the issuance of certain rights, options or warrants to holders of our common stock;

Not all Significant Restructuring Transactions will Constitute a Fundamental Change, in Which Case you Will not Have the Right to Require us to Repurchase May 2026 Convertible Notes and the June 2026 Convertible Notes for Cash.

 

If certain corporate events called “fundamental changes” occur, then, subject to a limited exception described in this prospectus, you will have the right to require us to repurchase your Notes for cash. However, the definition of “fundamental change” is limited to specific corporate events and does not include all events that may adversely affect our financial condition or the trading price of the Notes. For example, a leveraged recapitalization, refinancing, restructuring or acquisition by us may not constitute a fundamental change that would require us to repurchase the May 2026 Convertible Notes and the June 2026 Convertible Notes. Nonetheless, these events could significantly increase the amount of our indebtedness, harm our credit rating or adversely affect our capital structure and the trading price of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and the June 2026 Convertible Notes.

 

The Increase to the Conversion Rate Resulting from a Make-Whole Fundamental Change may not Adequately Compensate Noteholders for the Lost Option Value of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes. In addition, a Variety of Transactions that do not Constitute a Make-Whole Fundamental Change may Significantly Reduce the Option Value of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes Without a Corresponding Increase to the Conversion Rate.

 

If certain corporate events that constitute a “Make-Whole Fundamental Change” occur, then we will, in certain circumstances, temporarily increase the Conversion Rate of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes. The amount of the increase to the Conversion Rate of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes will depend on the date on which the Make-Whole Fundamental Change becomes effective and the applicable “stock price.” While the increase to the Conversion Rate is designed to compensate holders of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes for the lost option value of their Notes resulting from a Make-Whole Fundamental Change, the increase is only an approximation and may not adequately compensate Noteholders for the loss in option value. In addition, if the applicable “stock price” is greater than $300.00 per share or less than $40.20 per share (in each case, subject to adjustment), then we will not increase the conversion rate for May 2026 Convertible Notes for the make-whole fundamental change. Moreover, we will not increase the conversion rate for the May 2026 Convertible Notes pursuant to these provisions to an amount that exceeds 24.8750 shares of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock per $1,000 principal amount of Notes (plus accrued and unpaid interest), subject to adjustment. In addition, if the applicable “stock price” is greater than $400.00 per share or less than $68.73 per share (in each case, subject to adjustment), then we will not increase the conversion rate for June 2026 Convertible Notes for the make-whole fundamental change. Moreover, we will not increase the conversion rate for the June 2026 Convertible Notes pursuant to these provisions to an amount that exceeds 14.5496 shares of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock per $1,000 principal amount of Notes (plus accrued and unpaid interest), subject to adjustment.

Furthermore, the definition of make-whole fundamental change is limited to certain specific transactions. In addition, our obligation to increase the conversion rate in connection with a make-whole fundamental change could be considered a penalty, in which case its enforceability would be subject to general principles of reasonableness and equitable remedies.

Regulatory Actions, Changes in Market Conditions and Other Events may Adversely Affect the Trading Price and Liquidity of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes and the Ability of Investors to Implement a Convertible Note Arbitrage Trading Strategy.

 

We expect that many investors in the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes, including potential purchasers of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes from the original purchasers will seek to employ a convertible note arbitrage strategy. Under this strategy, investors typically short sell a certain number of shares of our common stock and adjust their short position over time while they continue to hold the Notes. Investors may also implement this type of strategy by entering into swaps on our common stock in lieu of, or in addition to, short selling shares of our common stock.

 

-47-

 

 

The SEC and other regulatory authorities have implemented various rules and taken certain actions, and may in the future adopt additional rules and take other actions, that may impact those engaging in short selling activity involving equity securities (including our common stock). These rules and actions include Rule 201 of SEC Regulation SHO, the adoption by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc., and the national securities exchanges of a “limit up-limit down” program, the imposition of market-wide circuit breakers that halt trading of securities for certain periods following specific market declines, and the implementation of certain regulatory reforms required by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010. Any governmental or regulatory action that restricts investors’ ability to effect short sales of our common stock or enter into equity swaps on our common stock could depress the trading price of, and the liquidity of the market for, the Notes.

 

In addition, the liquidity of the market for our common stock and other market conditions could deteriorate, which could reduce, or eliminate entirely, the number of shares available for lending in connection with short sale transactions and the number of counterparties willing to enter into an equity swap on our common stock with a note investor. These and other market events could make implementing a convertible note arbitrage strategy prohibitively expensive or infeasible. If investors in this offering or potential purchasers of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes that seek to employ a convertible note arbitrage strategy are unable to do so on commercial terms, or at all, then the trading price of, and the liquidity of the market for, the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes may significantly decline.

 

You May be Subject to Tax if we Adjust, or Fail to Adjust, the Conversion Rate of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes, even Though you Will not Receive a Corresponding Cash Distribution.

 

We will adjust the Conversion Rate of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes in certain circumstances, including the payment of cash dividends on our common stock. Adjustments (or failures to make adjustments) that have the effect of increasing your proportionate interest in our assets or earnings and profits may in some circumstances result in a deemed distribution, for U.S. federal income tax purposes, to you even though no cash or property is received. Adjustments to the conversion rate made pursuant to a bona fide, reasonable adjustment formula that has the effect of preventing the dilution of the interest of the holders of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes, however, will generally not be considered to result in a deemed distribution to you. In addition, if we do not adjust (or adjust adequately) the conversion rate after an event that increases your proportionate interest in us, then you could be treated as having received a deemed taxable dividend. For example, if we adjust the Conversion Rate May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes as a result of a distribution that is taxable to holders of our common stock, such as a cash dividend, then you may be deemed, for U.S. federal income tax purposes, to have received a taxable dividend to the extent of our earnings and profits, without the receipt of any cash or property. If a make-whole fundamental change occurs prior to the maturity date, under some circumstances, we will increase the conversion rate for May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes converted in connection with that make-whole fundamental change. Such increase may also be treated as a distribution subject to U.S. federal income tax as a dividend.

 

If you are subject to backup withholding, or if you are a non-U.S. holder (as defined in “Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Considerations”) subject to U.S. federal withholding tax, such withholding may be withheld from or set off against subsequent payments on the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes or our common stock owned by you or from any proceeds of any subsequent sale, exchange or other disposition of such Notes (including the retirement of such May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes) or such common stock or other funds or assets held by you. The Internal Revenue Service has issued proposed regulations addressing the amount and timing of deemed distributions, obligations of withholding agents and filing and notice obligations of issuers, which, if adopted, could affect the U.S. federal income tax treatment of a holder of Notes deemed to receive such a distribution.

 

-48-

 

 

A Rating Agency May not Rate the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes or May Assign a Rating that is Lower than Expected.

 

We do not intend to seek to have the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes rated by any rating agency. However, if one or more rating agencies rate the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes and assign a rating that is lower than the rating that investors expect, or reduce their rating in the future, then the trading price of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock and the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes could significantly decline.

 

In addition, market perceptions of our creditworthiness will directly affect the trading price of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes. Accordingly, if a ratings agency rates any of our indebtedness in the future or downgrades or withdraws the rating, or puts us on credit watch, then the trading price of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes will likely decline.

 

Provisions in the Indenture for Each of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes Could Delay or Prevent an Otherwise Beneficial Takeover of us.

 

Certain provisions in the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes and their respective Indenture could make a third-party attempt to acquire us more difficult or expensive. For example, if a takeover constitutes a fundamental change, then, holders of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes may have the right to require us to repurchase their Notes for cash. In addition, if a takeover constitutes a make-whole fundamental change, then we may be required to temporarily increase the conversion rate. In either case, and in other cases, our obligations under the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes and the indenture could increase the cost of acquiring us or otherwise discourage a third party from acquiring us, including in a transaction that noteholders or holders of our common stock may view as favorable.

 

You May Convert your May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes at any Time Prior to the Close of Business on the Second Business Day Immediately Preceding the Maturity Date for Such Notes, Subject to the Terms and Conditions of the Respective Indenture for such Notes, Including the Ownership Limitations Described Therein. The Trading Price of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes Could be Less than the Value of the Consideration into Which they Could Otherwise be Converted if Market Conditions or Other Factors Cause the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes to Trade at a Discount to Their Conversion Value.

 

Because the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes may be converted at any time prior to the close of business on the second business day immediately preceding their respective maturity dates, the value of the consideration a holder of such notes receives upon conversion will depend on the trading price of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock at the time of conversion. If the trading price of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock is below the conversion price of such notes at the time a holder elects to convert, such holder will receive shares of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock with a market value less than the principal amount of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes it is converting. There is no guarantee that the trading price of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock will exceed the conversion price at any time during the term of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes.

 

Fluctuations in the Trading Price of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock after a Holder Elects to Convert its May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes may Cause it to Receive less Valuable Consideration than Expected.

 

Upon conversion of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes, we will deliver shares of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock (together with cash in lieu of any fractional share) based on the applicable Conversion Rate. The number of shares of Class A Ordinary Common Stock a holder receive will be determined by the Conversion Rate in effect on the conversion date, subject to adjustment as described in the Indenture. We are required to deliver the settlement amount on the second trading day immediately following the relevant conversion date. Accordingly, if the trading price of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock declines between the conversion date and the date on which we deliver the settlement amount, you may receive shares of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock with a market value that is less than the value you anticipated at the time a holder elects to convert its May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes .

 

-49-

 

 

A Holders Investment in the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes may be Harmed if we Exercise our Forced Conversion Right.

 

We will have the right to force convert all or any portion of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes at any time on or after the date that is eighteen (18) months after the initial issue date and on or before the 20th VWAP trading day immediately before the maturity date, but only if (i) the daily VWAP of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock for at least 20 out of 30 consecutive VWAP trading days ending on, and including, the VWAP trading day immediately before the forced conversion notice date exceeds 200% of the conversion price; (ii) the daily dollar trading volume of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock for at least 20 out of 30 consecutive VWAP trading days ending on, and including, the VWAP trading day immediately before the forced conversion notice date is at least $50,000,000; and (iii) the Liquidity Conditions are satisfied. If we exercise our forced conversion right, then you may not be entitled to benefit from potential future appreciation in the trading price of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock beyond the respective Conversion Price for such Notes, and you may be unable to reinvest any proceeds from the conversion in comparable investments at favorable interest rates. In addition, a forced conversion of less than all of the outstanding May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes will likely harm the liquidity of the market for the unconverted Notes following the forced conversion. To the extent that the shares issuable upon a forced conversion would cause a holder to exceed the applicable restricted ownership percentage, we will instead issue pre-funded warrants exercisable for such excess shares.

 

The Accounting Method for the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes Could Adversely Affect our Reported Financial Condition and Results.

 

The accounting method for reflecting the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes on our balance sheet, accruing interest expense for the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes and reflecting the underlying shares of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock in our reported diluted earnings per share may adversely affect our reported earnings and financial condition.

 

In accordance with applicable accounting standards, we expect that the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes will be reflected as a liability on our balance sheets, with the initial carrying amount equal to the principal amount of the Notes, net of issuance costs. The issuance costs will be treated as a debt discount for accounting purposes, which will be amortized into interest expense over the term of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes. As a result of this amortization, the interest expense that we expect to recognize for the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes for accounting purposes will be greater than the cash interest payments we will pay on the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes, which will result in lower reported income.

 

In addition, we expect that the shares underlying the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes will be reflected in our diluted earnings per share using the “if converted” method. Under that method, diluted earnings per share would generally be calculated assuming that all the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes were converted solely into shares of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock at the beginning of the reporting period, unless the result would be anti-dilutive. The application of the if-converted method may reduce our reported diluted earnings per share, and accounting standards may change in the future in a manner that may adversely affect our diluted earnings per share.

 

Furthermore, if any of the conditions to the convertibility of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes is satisfied, then we may be required under applicable accounting standards to reclassify the liability carrying value of the Notes as a current, rather than a long-term, liability. This reclassification could be required even if no noteholders convert their May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes and could materially reduce our reported working capital.

 

We have not reached a final determination regarding the accounting treatment for the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes, and the description above is preliminary. Accordingly, we may account for the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes in a manner that is significantly different than described above.

 

Because the May 2026 Convertible Notes and the June 2026 Convertible Notes will Initially be Held in Book-Entry Form, Noteholders must Rely on DTC’s Procedures to Exercise their Rights and Remedies.

 

We initially issued the May 2026 Convertible Notes and the June 2026 Convertible Notes in the form of one or more “global notes” registered in the name of Cede & Co., as nominee of DTC. Beneficial interests in such global Notes will be shown on, and transfers of global notes will be effected only through, the records maintained by DTC. Except in limited circumstances, we will not issue certificated Notes. Accordingly, if you own a beneficial interest in a global note, then you will not be considered an owner or holder of such Notes. Instead, DTC or its nominee will be the sole holder of such Notes. Payments of principal, interest and other amounts on global Notes will be made to the paying agent, who will remit the payments to DTC. We expect that DTC will then credit those payments to the DTC participant accounts that hold book-entry interests in the global notes and that those participants will credit the payments to indirect DTC participants. Unlike persons who have certificated notes registered in their names, owners of beneficial interests in global notes will not have the direct right to act on our solicitations for consents or requests for waivers or other actions from noteholders. Instead, those beneficial owners will be permitted to act only to the extent that they have received appropriate proxies to do so from DTC or, if applicable, a DTC participant. The applicable procedures for the granting of these proxies may not be sufficient to enable owners of beneficial interests in global notes to vote on any requested actions on a timely basis.

 

Holding May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes will not, in Itself, Confer any Rights with Respect to our Class A Ordinary Common Stock.

 

Holders of May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes will generally not be entitled to any rights with respect to our Class A Ordinary Common Stock (including voting rights and rights to receive any dividends or other distributions on our Class A Ordinary Common Stock). However, such noteholders will be subject to all changes affecting our Class A Ordinary Common Stock to the extent the trading price of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes depends on the market price of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock and to the extent they receive shares of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock upon conversion of the May 2026 Convertible Notes and/or the June 2026 Convertible Notes. For example, if we propose an amendment to our charter documents that requires stockholder approval, then a noteholder will not, as such, be entitled to vote on the amendment, although the noteholder will be subject to any changes implemented by that amendment in the powers, preferences or special rights of our Class A Ordinary Common Stock.
